title: Surgical Mastery: Vitrectomy for Tractional Retinal Detachment (TRD)
summary: A comprehensive clinical and surgical guide to managing Tractional Retinal Detachment, primarily in the context of Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy (PDR). This poster covers pathophysiology, advanced dissection techniques, and evidence-based management protocols.

sections.title: Clinical Definition & Pathophysiology
sections.content: Tractional Retinal Detachment (TRD) is the separation of the neurosensory retina from the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) due to the pulling force of vitreoretinal membranes. In PDR, chronic ischemia leads to VEGF-mediated neovascularization. These vessels grow along the posterior hyaloid, forming fibrovascular proliferation (FVP). Over time, the fibrous component contracts, leading to tangential or anteroposterior traction and subsequent detachment without a primary break.

sections.title: Surgical Indications for TRD
content: Macula-involving TRD (most common indication).
Progressive TRD threatening the fovea.
Combined Tractional-Rhegmatogenous RD (TRRD).
Dense vitreous hemorrhage masking an underlying TRD.
Tight vitreoretinal traction causing macular edema unresponsive to anti-VEGF.

rows: Essential if media is opaque; identifies 'Table-top' configurations or tented retina.
Evaluates macular status, schisis vs. detachment, and vitreoretinal interface.
HbA1c optimization, Blood Pressure control, and Renal function (creatinine/GFR).
Injection of Bevacizumab (1.25mg) 2–7 days pre-op to regress FVP and reduce intraop bleeding.

sections.title: Surgical Step-by-Step Protocol
content: Step 1: Trocar placement (23G, 25G, or 27G) 3.5mm-4.0mm from limbus.
Step 2: Core Vitrectomy to clear hemorrhage and create space.
Step 3: Induction of Posterior Vitreous Detachment (PVD) using suction or a scraper (often difficult in TRD).
Step 4: Membrane Dissection (Segmentation and/or Delamination).
Step 5: Hemostasis using endodiathermy for bleeding fronds.
Step 6: Peripheral Shaving using depressed vitrectomy.
Step 7: Fluid-Air Exchange (FAX) and Endophotocoagulation (PRP completion).
Step 8: Tamponade selection (Air, Gas, or Silicone Oil).

rows: Vertical cutting of membranes into small islands to relieve tangential traction.
Horizontal dissection between the FVP and the internal limiting membrane.
Lifting the entire posterior hyaloid/membrane complex as a single unit.

sections.title: Intraoperative Red Flags
content: Iatrogenic Retinal Break (Peripheral or Posterior).
Massive Subretinal Hemorrhage (T-PA may be needed).
Inadvertent lens touch (Cataractogenesis).
Sudden Rise in IOP (Suprachoroidal Hemorrhage).

sections.title: Post-operative Management
content: Positioning: Face-down if gas/oil used.
IOP Monitoring: High risk of early post-op spikes (Neovascular Glaucoma).
Inflammation: Pred Forte 1% q1h to q4h; NSAIDs.
Fibrin Control: Consider subconjunctival steroids or intracameral TPA if fibrin is severe.

content.explanation: S: Segmentation, T: Traction removal, A: Anti-VEGF (Pre-op), S: Scissors (Delamination), S: Silicone Oil (Tamponade selection).

rows: Presence of a break, convex surface, rapid progression, moves with eye.
Shifting fluid, smooth surface, no tractional bands, inflammatory signs.
Inner layer elevation, non-mobile, asymptomatic unless extensive.

sections.title: Prognosis & Complications
content: Anatomic Success: >90% with modern instrumentation.
Visual Recovery: Limited by macular ischemia and chronicity of detachment.
NVI/NVG: Risk remains if ischemia is not treated with adequate laser.
Recurrent Hemorrhage: High in diabetic patients; consider 'oil under air' technique.

sections.title: Landmark Clinical Pearl
content: Avoid aggressive PVD induction over the macula if membranes are tight; instead, use 'Inside-Out' dissection starting from the optic nerve where the hyaloid is often already detached.

sections.title: Recent Advances
sections.content: Digitalized 3D visualization systems (NGENUITY/ARTEVO) allow for higher magnification and better depth of field during delicate delamination. High-speed vitrectomy (20,000 CPM) reduces vitreous turbulence, minimizing iatrogenic breaks during peripheral shaving.
